# Add a personal setting

A choice each person makes for themselves, such as which emails they get, in a tab of the account page, from a table, a resource and roles, with no UI code.

Rijnland's accountants want an email for each invoice that passes its due date; the warehouse would rather get none. That is a choice each person makes for themselves, so it belongs on their [account page](../reference/auth.md#account-page), and the fields the page shows come from a resource like any other. This guide adds it to the ERP example (`examples/erp`) in four steps: a table, a resource, roles and a tab.

## 1. A table with one row per person

The table is the app's own, keyed by the person's user id. With Better Auth the id is text, and a reference to `auth."user"` removes the row with its person. Each choice is a column with its default:

```sql title="db/migrations/021_notification_settings.sql"
-- Each person's choice of notification emails, one row per person, keyed by their Better Auth id. Someone who never
-- saved a choice has no row: read the default for them.
create table core.notification_settings (
  user_id text primary key references auth."user" (id) on delete cascade,
  overdue_invoices text not null default 'each' check (overdue_invoices in ('each', 'daily', 'never'))
);
```

Apply it with `bun run db:migrate`. A person has no row until they first save; the default stands for them until then.

## 2. A resource each person owns

The resource names the table, its fields and their defaults, and makes the key its owner with `.owner(...)`, so each person has one record of their own. The view gives the field its label, help and the words for its values, and keeps the resource out of the sidebar:

```ts title="config/notification_settings/data.ts"
import { f, resource } from '@protobase/schema'
import { erpAccess } from '../roles'

/** core.notification_settings: each person's own, shown by the account page's Notifications tab. */
export const notificationSettings = resource('notification_settings')
  .table('core.notification_settings')
  .fields({
    user_id: f.text(),
    overdue_invoices: f.enum(['each', 'daily', 'never']).default('each'),
  })
  .primaryKey((r) => r.user_id)
  .owner((r) => r.user_id)
  .access(erpAccess('notification_settings'))
```
```ts title="config/notification_settings/ui.ts"
import { view } from '@protobase/schema'
import type { notificationSettings } from './data'

export const notificationSettingsView = view<typeof notificationSettings>('notification_settings')
  .names({ singular: 'Notification setting', plural: 'Notification settings' })
  // Each person changes their own on the account page.
  .nav({ hidden: true })
  .fields((r) => ({
    overdue_invoices: r.overdue_invoices
      .label('Overdue invoices')
      .help('An email when an invoice passes its due date unpaid.')
      .valueLabels({ each: 'For each invoice', daily: 'Once a day', never: 'Never' }),
  }))
```

Export both from `config/index.ts`, as every resource is.

## 3. Roles that have settings

Give each role that should have the setting `.read.own`, `.create.own` and `.update.own` on the resource, in `config/roles.ts`:

```ts
const ownNotificationSettings = ['notification_settings.read.own', 'notification_settings.create.own', 'notification_settings.update.own'] as const

export const roles = defineRoles<ErpName>({
  admin: ['*'],
  auditor: ['*.read', ...ownNotificationSettings],
  sales: [...ownNotificationSettings, 'orders.read.own', ...],
  // the other roles alike: manager holds them already through '*.read', '*.create' and '*.update', and the
  // integration role, which is no person, has none
})
```

A role that may read but not write sees the choice without a control to change it; a role that may not read has no Notifications tab. Once a `Settings` block shows the resource, every caller reads and writes only their own record, an admin holding `*` included, in the block and in the API alike.

## 4. A tab on the account page

Export a page named `account` to replace the standard one: the standard tabs from `accountTabs`, in the order to show them, and a tab of your own with a [`Settings`](../reference/blocks.md#settings) block on the resource:

```tsx title="config/account.tsx"
/** @jsxImportSource @protobase/layout */
import { Page, Settings, Tab, Tabs, accountTabs, page } from '@protobase/layout'

/** The standard account page with a Notifications tab, where each person picks the emails they get. */
export const account = page(
  'account',
  <Page title="Account">
    <Tabs>
      {accountTabs.profile}
      {accountTabs.security}
      <Tab name="notifications" label="Notifications">
        <Settings resource="notification_settings" title="Emails" description="What the ERP emails you about." />
      </Tab>
      {accountTabs.devices}
      {accountTabs.apps}
    </Tabs>
  </Page>,
)
```

Export it from `config/index.ts` too. Open **Account** in the user menu and then **Notifications**, at `/-/account/notifications`: the choice shows as a select with its label and help, set to **For each invoice** until it changes. Picking another value saves it at once; the first save creates the person's row.

## Reading the choice

Code of your own, such as a job that sends the emails, reads the choice with SQL. Someone who never saved has no row, so read the default for them:

```sql
select u.email
from auth."user" u
left join core.notification_settings s on s.user_id = u.id
where coalesce(s.overdue_invoices, 'each') = 'each'
```

The [`Settings` block](../reference/blocks.md#settings) has its props, the field types it draws and the checks it runs at startup.
